data.targetWord: The Christian belief that God is three persons in one: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit

examples.en-GB: Christians baptise in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, expressing belief in the Trinity.

data.targetWord: The belief that God took human form in the person of Jesus Christ

examples.en-GB: Christmas celebrates the incarnation — God becoming a human baby.

data.targetWord: Jesus rising from the dead on Easter Sunday; a foundational belief in Christianity

examples.en-GB: Christians believe the resurrection proves that death is not the end.

data.targetWord: Being rescued from the consequences of sin and restored to a right relationship with God

examples.en-GB: Christians believe Jesus's death and resurrection made salvation possible for all people.

data.targetWord: God's free, undeserved love and gift to humanity — salvation cannot be earned

examples.en-GB: The concept of grace means humans receive God's love as a gift, not as a reward for good behaviour.

data.targetWord: Actions or attitudes that break the relationship between humans and God

examples.en-GB: Christians confess their sins in prayer and seek forgiveness.

data.targetWord: Meaning 'good news'; the message about Jesus; also the four Gospel books of the Bible (Matthew, Mark, Luke, John)

examples.en-GB: The Gospel of Mark is the shortest and possibly the oldest of the four Gospels.

data.targetWord: A short story Jesus used to teach about God's kingdom and how to live

examples.en-GB: The Parable of the Good Samaritan teaches that everyone is our neighbour.

data.targetWord: A ritual believed to communicate God's grace to believers

examples.en-GB: Baptism and Eucharist are the two sacraments accepted by most Christian denominations.

data.targetWord: A water ritual marking entry into the Christian community

examples.en-GB: Some Christians baptise babies; others wait until adults can make their own commitment.

data.targetWord: The ritual sharing of bread and wine, remembering Jesus's death and resurrection; also called Holy Communion or Mass

examples.en-GB: Catholics believe the bread and wine become the body and blood of Jesus during the Eucharist.

data.targetWord: A branch or tradition within Christianity, such as Catholic, Anglican, Baptist, or Orthodox

examples.en-GB: Different denominations have different views on baptism and the Eucharist.

data.targetWord: The Greek word for selfless, unconditional love; the highest form of love in Christian ethics

examples.en-GB: Christians are called to show agape — selfless love — even towards their enemies.

data.targetWord: Following Jesus and putting his teachings into practice in daily life

examples.en-GB: A disciple might read the Bible, serve the poor, and pray regularly as part of their discipleship.

data.targetWord: The four-week season of preparation and waiting before Christmas

examples.en-GB: During Advent, Christians light candles on an Advent wreath to mark the weeks before Christmas.

data.targetWord: The forty-day Christian season of fasting, reflection, and repentance before Easter

examples.en-GB: During Lent, many Christians give up something as a form of fasting and self-discipline.

data.targetWord: The Christian festival fifty days after Easter celebrating the coming of the Holy Spirit and the birth of the Church

examples.en-GB: At Pentecost the disciples received the Holy Spirit and began to proclaim the Gospel boldly.

data.targetWord: Expressing love, honour, and devotion to God through prayer, singing, scripture, and service

examples.en-GB: Christians worship through prayer, singing hymns, reading the Bible, and serving others.

data.targetWord: The Hebrew word meaning 'anointed one'; Christians believe Jesus is the promised Messiah who restores humanity's relationship with God

examples.en-GB: The word 'Christ' is the Greek translation of Messiah — Jesus Christ means Jesus the Anointed One.

data.targetWord: The belief that Jesus's death on the cross paid the penalty for human sin, restoring the broken relationship between humanity and God

examples.en-GB: Good Friday marks the crucifixion — the act of atonement central to Christian salvation belief.

data.targetWord: The prayer Jesus taught his disciples, covering praise, petition, forgiveness, and trust in God

examples.en-GB: The Lord's Prayer begins 'Our Father in heaven' and is used in Christian worship worldwide.

data.targetWord: The first part of the Christian Bible, containing Jewish scriptures including Law, history, poetry, and prophecy

examples.en-GB: The Old Testament is shared with Judaism; Christians read it as pointing towards Jesus.

data.targetWord: The second part of the Christian Bible, containing the four Gospels, Acts, Letters, and Revelation

examples.en-GB: The New Testament records Jesus's life, teaching, and the growth of the early Church.

data.targetWord: The belief in one God; Christianity, Islam, and Judaism are all monotheistic religions

examples.en-GB: Although Christians believe in the Trinity, they are monotheists — they believe in one God.

data.targetWord: The inner sense of right and wrong, which Christians believe is guided by the Holy Spirit

examples.en-GB: A Christian might consult their conscience, alongside the Bible and Church teaching, when making ethical decisions.
